subject.title: Feature: Handle Signal message edits (editMessage envelope)

question: What Signal `editMessage` behavior should OpenClaw guarantee for transcript state and reply triggering?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but replacement versus marker-only handling and non-mentioned group edit replies are user-visible session semantics that automation should not choose alone.

options.title: Implement Signal-local edit semantics
options.body: Type `targetSentTimestamp`, preserve edit metadata or an `[edited]` marker, update or dedupe against the original message under a documented policy, and suppress non-mentioned group edit replies.

options.title: Defer to lifecycle umbrella
options.body: Keep this issue blocked until https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/55691 defines shared edit/delete/recall lifecycle semantics across channels.

options.title: Accept marker-only scope
options.body: Only mark edited Signal messages for now and leave transcript replacement, cancellation, and reply suppression for later product work.

recommendation.title: Implement Signal-local edit semantics
recommendation.body: Type `targetSentTimestamp`, preserve edit metadata or an `[edited]` marker, update or dedupe against the original message under a documented policy, and suppress non-mentioned group edit replies.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has the strongest current history on the Signal inbound and channel-routing code paths where the behavior would live.
